lines: Based on these policies and the revision of the earnings target, MUFG has revised its year-end dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 from ¥48.00 to ¥52.00 per share.
As a result, the annual dividend for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 is forecast to be ¥100.00 per share.

desk.headline: Half-year profit up 26% to ¥1.63tn; full-year profit target raised to ¥2.8tn and dividend forecast lifted to ¥100

other.label: Profits attributable to owners of parent

results: Profit attributable to shareholders rose 26% to ¥1.63tn in the six months to September, from ¥1.29tn a year earlier.
Gross profits grew 18% to ¥3.45tn and net operating profits 29% to ¥1.69tn; diluted EPS rose to ¥144.40 from ¥112.77.
MUFG credited steady progress in its customer businesses and higher equity-method earnings from its Morgan Stanley stake.
Interim dividend of ¥48 per share; share buybacks in the half came to ¥100bn, against ¥250bn a year earlier.
Common equity tier 1 ratio stood at a preliminary 12.65% at end-September.

guidance.summary: MUFG raised its full-year profit target by ¥100bn to ¥2.8tn and lifted its year-end dividend forecast from ¥48 to ¥52, taking the annual dividend to ¥100. It keeps a payout target of about 40%.

items.metric: Profits attributable to owners of parent

points: The company tied the higher target to about ¥100bn more ordinary profit, from customer segments and Morgan Stanley-related equity earnings.
Dividend policy stays at about 40% payout, aiming for steady per-share increases through profit growth.
Press coverage noted MUFG's data centre lending exposure of ¥3.3tn out of ¥180tn total credit exposure, as peers flagged a possible slowdown in data centre investment.
call.source: Company notice on revised targets (6-K, 13 Nov 2026) and The Edge Malaysia, 13 Nov 2026; no direct management quotes found

watch: Progress toward the ¥2.8tn profit target in the second half.
Whether a new share buyback is announced; none was stated in the filings read.
Credit quality in data centre lending as the sector slows.
